_: Curated history of notable companies headquartered or founded in specific NYC buildings, keyed by BIN. Multiple entries per building are listed in chronological order.

1015862.name: Empire State Inc. (the building's holding company itself)
1015862.note: The Empire State Building was famously underleased through the 1930s — nicknamed the 'Empty State Building' — but its observation deck and licensing income kept it solvent. Today the building alone is worth roughly $2 billion.

1036156.name: Chrysler Corporation (original)
1036156.note: The Chrysler Building was Walter Chrysler's personal investment, not a corporate HQ — he financed it with his own money so his children could inherit it. Chrysler Corp leased and used the upper floors but never owned the building.

1088469.name: Condé Nast
1088469.note: Condé Nast (Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ) is the anchor tenant at One World Trade Center, occupying floors 20–44 since 2014.
